description: Banded iron formation (Superior and Algoma types): chert–iron-oxide sheets of the 2.6–1.85 Ga acme, inherited in cratonic basement when the timeline starts after it.

any_of.note: inherited Paleoproterozoic BIF in the basement (plan §8.6)
Superior-type BIF on passive-margin shelves (Bekker et al. 2010)

notes: Sizing: USGS Bulletin 1693 (Cox & Singer eds. 1986) model 34a, Superior Fe, n = 66: tonnage 11 / 170 / 2400 Mt (Fig. 172, p. 229) and Fe 30 / 53 / 66 % (Fig. 173, p. 230), figure intercepts. The model covers Algoma-type too (model 28b, p. 198: its grade–tonnage model 'is included under Superior Fe'). The 53 % Fe median is well above primary iron formation (typically 30–35 % Fe, OFR 95-831), so the model probably includes enriched ores. See crates/deeptime-core/data/usgs/bif_fe.json.

PLACEHOLDERS (not found in any USGS source): ore_density_t_m3 3.6 (hematite–magnetite–quartz rock), density_per_1e5km2 1 / 4 / 12, min_separation_m 5000, formation_depth_m 1200 (for an inherited sheet: its depth at the timeline's start, which slow cratonic erosion then brings towards the surface).
formation_time cause: an inherited deposit takes the time of its causing event (the BIF shelf sea), not a frame of the timeline.
Design values: the curves, clustering, zoning, aspect and dip (folded iron formation), size multipliers.
Create stones (decisions file): banded_iron_formation (crimsite → iron) is the preferred host at 2.0 and the sheet's own rock class.
